stands.resumo: November Rain (ノーヴェンバー・レイン（11月の雨）, Nōvenbā Rein) is the Stand of Jodio Joestar, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: ノーヴェンバー・レイン（11月の雨）

namesake.texto: November Rain (Guns N' Roses song) | Novem ("Nine" in Latin)

Appearance: November Rain has a humanoid head and broad torso attached to a downward-pointing cone. Its face and neck are heavily creased with lines converging in the center of its face. It has a light, concave plate of armor covering the center of its face and neck, serrated at the top of its head. The armor is curved inward at its eyes and neck to leave them exposed, giving November Rain an angry expression. The armor also has a slit on each side below its eyes, small holes beneath the slits near its chin, and a single hole on its forehead. Oval-shaped armor covers each side of its head, split into three pieces. The irises of its eyes are split by vertical lines.

November Rain's torso is plain, but feather-like appendages project from the cone at its stomach. The cone itself is grooved horizontally, splitting it into four parts. It bears two congruent triangles connected to each other that are split between a dark and bright half, matching the symbol on Jodio's outfit.

Finally, November Rain possesses four long thin legs, with two emerging from the front out of its shoulders, and the other two from its back. Each leg is articulated with ball joints, and its front legs are thicker than the back.
Color Schemes
Abilities: Rain Generation

November Rain is able to produce localized rain showers within a radius of 3 meters of Jodio's body and a height of 4 meters; any supernatural properties held by the raindrops are lost upon contact with the surface of a body of water unless the rain comes in contact with an object on the water's surface first. The rain usually falls parallel to Jodio's own head-to-toe axis, which he can take advantage of by changing the orientation of his body with respect to the ground; while ensnared upside down by Wild Cat Size's Stand Cat Size, he is able to swing his body such that he is perpendicular to the ground and then direct November Rain's to make it rain horizontally.

November Rain is also not limited to the outdoors, as it can produce rain within localized areas such as the interior of a building, a vehicle, a suitcase, or even inside Jodio's mouth. Jodio has also shown the ability to direct the path of a single raindrop with a high degree of precision, successfully guiding it to attack a single instance of Bags' Groove hiding in Dragona Joestar's right lung from their mouth, and without harming Dragona at all.
Heavy Rain

Jodio can alter the force exerted by the raindrops produced by November Rain, making them seem to be unnaturally heavy, as well as selectively choose what is affected by the increased weight. Its concentrated downpours are able to non-lethally incapacitate a couple of Honolulu Police Officers attempting to harass Jodio and Dragona, while later leaving them unharmed; and soak through the carpet of Rohan Kishibe's Hawai'i villa and destroy the underlying concrete floor. The rain can also be lethal, having the strength to pierce through flesh and bone.

Jodio can also use this property defensively by creating a protective barrier around himself with a rain shower of dense raindrops; this has worked both on Cat Size's wires and bullets controlled by Glory Days.

The supernatural properties of the water produced by November Rain extend beyond its 3-meter radius; despite Bobby Jean having deduced the Stand's range and keeping his distance from Jodio during their fight in the Pearl General Hospital restroom, a drop of November Rain's water that had been splattered onto the ceiling lands on Bobby Jean's head and pierces through his skull, killing him instantly. The supernatural properties are also retained if the rain comes in contact with something floating on water, such as the vinyl balls Hacca Howler has in the pool on his megayacht; Jodio uses the balls to clog the drain to prevent Key West and West End Girl from escaping and uses his rain to pierce through the balls and into West End Girl, wounding Key West.

stands.resumo: Smooth Operators (スムース・オペレイターズ, Sumūsu Opereitāzu) is the Stand of Dragona Joestar, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: スムース・オペレイターズ

Appearance: Smooth Operators is a group of four small robot-like Stands. Each "operator" has the appearance of a small robot with a humanoid head and torso and tank treads instead of legs. Their heads have an oblong shape with curved corners, with the front part elongated like a nose. They also have two mechanical eyes protruding from the top of their heads. Their shoulders are cylindrical and their arms have artificial articulations. Finally, each operator has a stylized "SO" engraved on the top of the head.
Color Schemes
Personality: Although they don't regularly talk, Smooth Operators is capable of saying words and reacting to events, as one of them replies "OK!" to Dragona's announcement of the team's plan and they all scream "Ah!" when thrown off of a surface. Beyond single-word responses, they are also capable of saying short phrases such as calling out their own name.
Additionally, Smooth Operators occasionally grunts "ISHI! ISHI! ISHI!" (イシ! イシ! イシ!) and "Ushi Ushi" (ウシ ウシ) when using their ability.
Abilities: Surface Displacement

Smooth Operators enables Dragona to "slide" things across two-dimensional planes, regardless of that thing being a physical object or a physical feature on the object. Dragona has used the Stand to move numbers around on a car license plate, photographs on a driver's license, a fingerprint on a tablet computer onto its fingerprint scanner, and a human's facial features. The Stand has also been used to invert a vinyl ball, with no permanent damage to the affected objects or people. Dragona is initially shown being in physical contact with the objects affected by Smooth Operators, often directing Smooth Operators in a specific direction. Later, Smooth Operators is shown acting without instruction.

Smooth Operators can also operate on human bodies, giving Dragona various ways to treat injuries. Dragona can completely displace a wound (as long as it is no deeper than 7 millimeters) by transferring it onto an inanimate object, which subsequently shatters. For example, Smooth Operators moves wounds inflicted as a result of middle school bullying from Dragona's chest onto a soup spoon, and also transfers a bleeding neck wound onto a wine bottle. Alternatively, Dragona can use the Stand for makeshift first aid by having Smooth Operators grab the edges of an open laceration and slide the skin together to close the wound. However, Dragona notes that because the Stand only affects the surface layer, this method acts more like a temporary suture and cannot completely stop internal bleeding if a deeper blood vessel is severed.

The Stand's ability to manipulate objects is constrained by the collective physical strength of the Smooth Operators units. For instance, Dragona notes that it is difficult for the Stand to crack the safe in Rohan's villa because the metal bars comprising the lock mechanism are too heavy for the small units to move.

stands.resumo: The Hustle (THE(ザ)ハッスル, Za Hassuru) is the Stand of Paco Laburantes, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: The Hustle (Van McCoy and the Soul City Symphony single)[a]

Appearance: The Hustle manifests as an integrated ability for Paco, typically appearing as his muscles bulging out or vibrating.
Abilities: Prehensile Muscles

The Hustle morphs Paco's muscles to bulge and be able to grab onto things that touch the surface of his body, such as with the backs of his hands or his elbows. He can easily swipe objects such as wallets without even needing to move the joints in his fingers. Jodio describes Paco's muscles as being similar to when people tense up their muscles to trap mosquitoes sucking blood. For example, he is capable of trapping his enemy's limbs or weapons in his muscles.

The Stand allows Paco to be versatile with his movements, as he can hang from a ceiling vent or climb a tree using his back muscles. He can also grab an object such as a chair with his back and throw it at the enemy without using his hands.
Muscle Vibration

The precise control The Hustle gives Paco over his musculature allows him to reshape his body a little and vibrate his muscles independently. He is first seen demonstrating this ability when trapped by Cat Size's wires, as he uses a scissor blade that he manages to wedge between the wire and his ankle and vibrates his muscles to saw through it. The vibration also appears to increase his physical strength, as he announces "Do the HUSTLE" before he begins to vibrate his muscles in the fight against Charming Man.

Paco can also transfer this muscular vibration onto other people through physical contact, either directly with the target or with an object held by the target. He can use it to protect his allies by controlling their muscles to bulge, such as when he lightly punches Jodio's back to bulge his neck muscles and prevent a deep knife wound. The Hustle can also cause its target's muscles to begin to unnaturally convulse and expand, immobilizing the affected area. This is demonstrated in the fight with Charming Man, where Paco grabs onto the blade of Charming Man's knife with the back of his forearm before he punches his own arm, sending the muscle vibrations through the knife's blade and through Charming Man's hand and forearm.
Muscle Toughness

Additionally, the extreme density and toughness of Paco's muscles can be utilized as both a defensive and offensive measure. Because of how hard he can tense them, attackers can severely injure themselves upon striking him. For instance, when Paco's father punches him, he ends up hurting his own fist against Paco's body. Similarly, when an alligator violently bites down on Paco's arm, the sheer hardness of his muscles completely shatters the animal's row of teeth.

stands.resumo: THE MATTEKUDASAI (THE MATTEKUDASAI(ザ・マッテクダサイ), Za Mattekudasai, lit. "THE PLEASEWAIT") is the Stand of Usagi Alohaoe, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: THE MATTEKUDASAI(ザ・マッテクダサイ)

Appearance: THE MATTEKUDASAI is a mechanical bird-like Stand of variable size, with most of its default state appearances showing it being as big as a domestic cat or smaller. It has a bulbous body with a small forked tail as well as flat tear-shaped arms, which end in small digits that allow THE MATTEKUDASAI to grab onto objects or scale walls. It has humanoid mechanical legs with round knees and three large digits on each foot. It also bears Usagi's symbol on its chest, which resembles the outstretched arms of the Stand in a V shape. Its shoulder, hips, and ears have round studs grooved across the middle, as well as a semi-circle engraved on the rear-pointing side.
THE MATTEKUDASAI has a round head and is equipped with a mask which has the rough shape of a semi-cylinder with pointed fins at the end, as well as a flat front side and two large oval blank eyes.
THE MATTEKUDASAI appears to move by hopping on the ground like passerine birds.

Finally, its size has varied throughout the story, excluding transformations. During its first appearance, THE MATTEKUDASAI could fit in the palm of Usagi's hand. In a later chapter, it is shown to be slightly larger than Usagi's head.

After the time skip the top of its head became flatter, making it resemble a rectangular prism with a semi-cylinder bottom, and the pointed fins of its mask appear to be considerably longer. Later in the story, THE MATTEKUDASAI's feet grow bigger and start to resemble rabbit paws.
Color Schemes
Personality: THE MATTEKUDASAI often cries like "NYUUUUUN" or "NYUUUUMU" when activating its ability. It is also capable of saying its name, "MATTE KUDASAI", when asking someone to wait.
Abilities: Desired Object Transformation
Fake Properties

The objects that THE MATTEKUDASAI transforms into are notably fake copies of other objects, but they still operate how the original does with no issue. The "fakeness" is first displayed during the burglary at Rohan's Villa when Usagi has Dragona wish for a security camera which THE MATTEKUDASAI transforms into, partially merging with one of the actual security cameras in order to send a false second video feed to the security system where all of their appearances are drastically altered. This trick is used again when visiting the Hawaii State Land Registry Office to view the original copies of HOWLER Company's deeds to the slopes of Hualalai. THE MATTEKUDASAI can even transform into something as large as a fake room wrapped around a real room in order to conceal it, faking the sounds that leak outside the walls of the Stand.

THE MATTEKUDASAI can also increase its own complexity as a result of other's wishes. While being attacked by Bags' Groove, Usagi asks Dragona to wish for a straw so he can perform an emergency thoracostomy on himself. Later, as Charming Man uses his Stand Big Mouth Strikes Again to search inside Usagi's lungs, he idly says how he cannot see anything due to how dark it is, prompting THE MATTEKUDASAI to add working lights to the end of the straw.

stands.resumo: Big Mouth Strikes Again (ビッグマウス・ストライクス・アゲイン, Biggumausu Sutoraikusu Agein) is the Stand of Charming Man, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: ビッグマウス・ストライクス・アゲイン

Appearance: Big Mouth Strikes Again is an integrated ability that affects Charming Man's body, which naturally has a rough, sand-like texture. Charming Man states that while his skin texture is shared among his village, his Stand is his own unique ability. His skin can float around him when he is using his powers, appearing like small sand and rock fragments. When it transforms Charming Man to resemble Paco Laburantes, the real Paco notes that the fragments have different colors.
Abilities: Skin Dispersion

Big Mouth Strikes Again uses the deepest basal layer of Charming Man's sand-like skin. The cells produced there are pushed upward from the dermis toward the epidermis, repeating this movement from one layer of skin to the next. Over the course of this accelerated skin cell turnover, his skin gradually hardens, taking about 45 seconds in total. The surface then becomes a fine, stone-like layer that he can shift and stack along his body.

Big Mouth Strikes Again allows Charming Man to move these hardened layers of skin around him, crumbling into particles like puzzle pieces. This makes him capable of dispersing pieces of his body to evade injuries, or pinning down enemies like Bags' Groove and pulling them away using the skin particles. He can even detach body parts like his eyeball and then disperse it into small particles to scout remotely. For example, he has his eyeball crumble into a straw to enter Usagi Alohaoe's body, and then has it regain its shape so he could search within the body for investigative purposes.

The effective range of his skin is a little over ten centimeters from the surface of his body, revolving around him like a satellite. However, his Stand is still capable of moving further than that, as Charming Man's eyeball travels deep inside Usagi's body.
Transformation and Camouflage

stands.resumo: Heaven's Door (ヘブンズ・ドアー, Hebunzu Doā) is the Stand of Rohan Kishibe, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: Heaven's Door (Part 4 Stand) | Knockin' on Heaven's Door (Bob Dylan song)

type.texto: Close-Range | Psychological Assault | Reconnaissance | Natural Humanoid

Appearance: Heaven's Door appears as a small boy resembling the protagonist of Rohan's manga, Pink Dark Boy. It wears a long overcoat. Its eyes lack irises and are vertically segmented with lines. There is also an outline around its eyes which extend downward onto its cheeks in a straight line, curving inward at the tips. Heaven's Door wears a bowler hat with transparent, checkered holes.
Color Schemes
Abilities: Book Transmutation

Heaven's Door is a close-range Stand that can turn any living being into books, pages unfurling from their bodies in the shape of whatever body part it opens from (for example, if from the face, the shape of the pages is of the person's entire face). Rohan seemingly has to touch the target with his hands to activate the effect, as Paco could restrain Rohan by the wrist and not get affected. The ability would activate in the area he touched, but also can spread elsewhere. For instance, Rohan touches Paco's forearm, causing his whole arm to unfurl into pages as well as his face. The effect does not have to activate right away. Rohan touches Dragona's hand, but the hand only unfurls into pages a few moments later.

The contents of the books contain information Rohan can read about the target, such as their name, age, personality, history, and motives. If one's face is turned into a book, they may be incapacitated while under the effect if Rohan wills it.

stands.resumo: Eclipse Eight (エクリプス8(エイト), Ekuripusu Eito) is the Stand of Hacca Howler, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: Eclipse (Pink Floyd song) | Eight (Hacca is the 8th generation head of the Howler family)

Appearance: Eclipse Eight is humanoid, with its body patterned in cracked, stone-like textures. Its face is mostly smooth except for the center, where a mask-like faceplate with the same cracked texture covers its mouth, runs horizontally beneath its eyes, and continues vertically around the top of its head. At the top, the faceplate rises into a mohawk-like rectangular ridge. Multiple circular, rivet-like studs line the sides of its head. The faceplate also has oval-shaped bumps near the center of its face and on its forehead. Its eyes are narrow and divided by vertical lines. A long, rod-like spike protrudes from each side of its head, with a large sphere beneath each spike near its cheeks.

Eclipse Eight wears a long coat with a wavy, ruffle-like collar and slightly tattered sleeves. Its shoulders are covered by smooth pauldrons that end in opposing curved points above and below. Around its waist is a curved, belt-like element, while the coat extends past it and reaches the ankles. Its knees feature downward-facing crescent shapes, and it wears shoes.
Color Schemes
Abilities: Mist Generation

The full extent of Eclipse Eight's abilities are unknown but it appears to be able to produce a mist only visible to Stand users from which it attacks using an unknown energy; however, neither Jodio, Dragona, nor Charming Man are able to truly perceive what Eclipse Eight does when they witness its abilities on board Howler's Megayacht. Despite having his hands and feet tied up by a team of U.S. Marine sailors sent to arrest him, Eclipse Eight's mist seemingly enables Howler to pick up a ballpoint pen located several feet away from him, which he soon drops to the deck of his ship through the summoned mist. The pen then bounces at great speed directly into the neck of one of the sailors who begins firing his machine gun uncontrollably; in the confusion, Howler and Eclipse Eight disappear without a trace, the sailor has died, and as the mist clears Dragona realizes that somehow Howler had managed to sign the documents transferring ownership of his family's land on Hualalai over to them.

stands.resumo: Cat Size (キャット・サイズ, Kyatto Saizu) is the Stand of Wild Cat Size, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

Appearance: Cat Size is an integrated ability that applies to the fur of the cats. The fur appears as long thin translucent strings akin to a fishing line.
Color Schemes
Abilities: Constricting Wires

Cat Size allows the three cats to create long thin translucent strings from their fur. The wires are hard to see and are compared to fishing line. Despite feeling as if it is made from natural materials, the wires are as durable as stainless steel and cannot be cut normally with scissors. The wires can target individual limbs but can be avoided, as Usagi Alohaoe was able to dodge an attack by jumping above one.

Once a wire is wrapped around a limb, it automatically ties itself off and tightens, digging into the victim's flesh. The nature of the wire and how it gets tighter on its own makes it very difficult to remove. Instead of wrapping around someone, the wire can also pierce through them and sew itself into their bodies.

Although the wires cannot be cut through ordinary means, it is still possible to remove them using other Stand abilities. For example, Smooth Operators dislocates Dragona's thumb and slides it down their wrist to place it below the string, allowing Dragona's hand to be thin enough for the string to easily slide off. The Hustle is also capable of allowing Paco to be freed from the trap by combining a scissor blade with the force of Paco's vibrating muscles to push the blade upward and break through it. When a wire is removed from its target, if a cat loses its concentration, or if it goes far enough from the Stand's range, it dissipates.
The cats can also work together to combine their wires to form a net for capturing their targets. Dragona hypothesizes that this ability was designed to help them capture and devour their prey.

stands.resumo: Bags' Groove (バグス・グルーヴ, Bagusu Gurūvu) is the Stand of Lulu, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

namesake.texto: Bags' Groove (Miles Davis song and album)

mangadebut.texto: TJL Chapter 14 (Ability only) | TJL Chapter 15 (1st full debut)

Appearance: Bags' Groove has a microscopic size, small enough to travel through blood vessels in a human body. It has a somewhat humanoid form wrapped in bandages which cover much of its body and head, giving it a mummified look. The head of the Stand resembles a helmet and has antennae ending in round bulbs. There is an opening for its thin eyes, which lack irises and are vertically segmented with lines. Below its eyes, the helmet has a downward-pointing arrow on the center of its face. There are also arrows extending from the sides of its face to its chin.

It has armor-like elements like a chestplate with shoulder pads. Additionally, it has sharp claws and three fingers. Its legs have knee pads, with the lower portion splitting into three legs wearing boots that are dark on top, making it appear as if it has dark toenails. On its back is a shield-like appendage pointing downwards, resembling an insect's pronotum. The center of that appendage wraps around the Stand's waist like a belt and the top of it is connected to the back of its head with a hose. It also has circles on the sides of its shoulders and hips.
Color Schemes
Personality: As an automatic Stand, Bags' Groove indiscriminately attacks anyone who would touch the object it is bound to. On occasion, the Stand emits a screech of "Bisshaa!" (ビッシャア) or "Busshaa!" (ブッシャアアッ).
Abilities: Bags' Groove is a long-distance, automatic pursuit-type ability with a colony form. Lulu can set up booby traps with Bags' Groove on any object of her choosing, such as the original hard copies of HOWLER's land deeds held at the Hawaii State Land Registry Office or pieces of a figurine. When another person comes into contact with the trigger object, a microscopic instance of Bags' Groove automatically infiltrates their body. A single object planted with Bags' Groove can trigger multiple times, as both Sophie White and Usagi Alohaoe begin to exhibit the symptoms of Bags' Groove's attacks after they both had touched the hard copies of HOWLER's land deeds.

As it is a remotely operated Stand, it is extremely physically weak and slow; Charming Man is able to catch and hold down Bags' Groove infiltrating Usagi using Big Mouth Strikes Again on his own eyeball without much difficulty. It is also susceptible to Lulu's emotional state, as once she breaks down in tears upon seeing Bobby Jean's dead body, the many iterations of Bags' Groove attacking Jodio, Usagi, and Sophie White return to her, and the victims all recover from the Stand's effects.
Lesion Infliction

With its microscopic size, Bags' Groove damages its victim's internal organs and causes a series of symptoms that — unless it is defeated — will result in the victim's death. The external symptoms vary and progressively worsen based on the Stand's continuous attacks. Bags' Groove's injuries are only permanent if it remains in its victim's body. If Bags' Groove succeeds in killing its victim, the cause of death appears to be nothing more than a disease. If Bags' Groove is removed, the lesions can be repaired and the various symptoms it causes will go into remission.

As an automatic Stand, Bags' Groove follows a set procedure for its attacks. It first travels to the victim's right lung where it makes a hole in the pulmonary artery to inflict a pulmonary edema, causing the victim to vomit up a cloudy fluid and obstruct their breathing, with victims saying it feels as if they are drowning; an emergency thoracostomy will relieve these symptoms, restoring their ability to breathe. The Stand may also cause its targets to break out in a rock-like rash on their necks. Afterwards, Bags' Groove travels toward the victim's brain through their blood vessels, eventually causing blood to spray out from the eyes, at which point only magnetic resonance imaging would be a means to identify where the Stand is inside its victim's body.

In addition to coming into contact with the boobytrapped physical object, Bags' Groove can also inflict its powers on others by coming into contact with it directly. When Charming Man uses his Stand to send his right eyeball into Usagi's body and then uses it to hold Bags' Groove down, he begins to suffer from a sudden tumorous growth in his right eye socket; he describes it as an average tumor which is painless, but it soon causes his health to deteriorate. This effect appears to be reversed once physical contact ceases.

stands.resumo: Glory Days (グローリー・デイズ, Gurōrī Deizu) is the Stand of Bobby Jean, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

Appearance: Glory Days works as an integrated ability for Bobby Jean, thus having no physical appearance. When activated, the bullets it affects gain a glow and halo.
Color Schemes
Abilities: Bullet Speed Manipulation

Glory Days allows Bobby Jean to control the speed of the bullets he fires from his mundane pistol equipped with a silencer, striking his targets without them realizing that a gun was ever fired and allowing him to collect any used cartridges to hide all evidence of his gunshots. The bullets can still only move in a straight line, but can be fired at a slower speed. Jodio Joestar and his allies are able to perceive the bullets slowly traveling toward them, but are unable to dodge in time before being struck. Upon hitting their targets, the bullets slowly dig into their bodies at the same angle they impacted. As such, without an effective Stand for defense, Glory Days is dangerously lethal.

Additionally, Glory Days can be utilized preemptively to prevent ambushes, as seen when Jodio attempts to ambush Bobby Jean but is cut short by slowed down bullets that Bobby Jean shot behind himself prior to Jodio's attack. Furthermore, the Stand's capabilities make it effective at trapping and cornering enemies as seen when Bobby Jean left bullets behind in an elevator to attack Paco. Its trapping expertise was also seen when used to completely swarm Jodio with bullets from different angles due to their slower speed allowing Bobby Jean to fire from multiple directions before the shots land.

stands.resumo: Lyin' Eyes (偽(いつわ)りの瞳(ひとみ) Lyin' Eyes, Itsuwari no Hitomi) is the Stand of Laem Chabang, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: 偽(いつわ)りの瞳(ひとみ) Lyin' Eyes

Appearance: Lyin' Eyes has no appearance, as it manifests as an integrated ability for Laem Chabang. It is depicted by showing the nematodes on her sunglasses.
Color Schemes
Abilities: Nematode Manipulation

Lyin' Eyes allows Laem Chabang to control nematodes that she raises as pets and has them live on her sunglasses. She has trained these nematodes to detect the stress pheromones given off by human beings, and they form specific patterns depending on the situation.

When Laem Chabang and Ningbo are first introduced to Hacca Howler by Key West, Lyin' Eyes reacts to Howler silently feeling fear at the potential loss of his family's fortune, and the nematodes form a map of the immediate vicinity with a specific focus on Howler's location with respect to her. During her interrogation of Meryl Mei Qi, Laem asks her simple "yes" or "no" questions; when Meryl lies or refuses to answer the nematodes detect her stress and form large piles on the lenses of Laem's sunglasses but when she is truthful the nematodes disperse.

stands.resumo: 200 Balloons (200(トゥハンドレッド)バルーンズ, Tuhandoreddo Barūnzu) is the Stand of Ningbo, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: 200(トゥハンドレッド)バルーンズ

Appearance: 200 Balloons is humanoid with an overweight, lumpy build shaped like a balloon. Its head is rounded, wearing a cap with a diamond-shaped protrusion on the top. The cap has open slits above its eyes, pointing toward the center. A small, dark circle is also present on the bottom center of its cap. Its large, oval-shaped eyes are segmented and it has a smile. The Stand notably has prominently puffed, balloon-like cheeks, which appear inflated.

A dark vertical mark runs down the center of its forehead, stopping at the center of its face. The vertical mark starts again below its mouth to its chin. It has a plain body, segmented forearms resembling puffer jacket sleeves, circular knuckle markings, knee pads, and boots. Its legs are very short compared to the length of its arms.
Color Schemes
Abilities: Inflation

200 Balloons possesses the ability to inflate objects or living beings that Ningbo touches. Otherwise inelastic objects swell up with some sort of gas less dense than the surrounding air, causing them to float. The effect also makes the object just as fragile as a balloon and prone to popping, subjecting inanimate objects to imminent destruction and living victims to dismemberment. The blast radius is presumed to be about 5 cm. This ability can be used defensively, turning otherwise dangerous objects such as bullets into harmless balloons.

Ningbo first uses it to destroy part of Meryl Mei Qi's computer keyboard in her school office before using it on her hand, causing it to swell up and lift her off the ground. When Paco Laburantes and Usagi Alohaoe head to her office they find her severed fingers, as Ningbo had then focused his Stand's ability on her knuckles to specifically injure her fingers as part of his and Laem Chabang's interrogation.

stands.resumo: West End Girl (ウエスト・エンド・ガール, Uesuto Endo Gāru) is the Stand of Key West, featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: ウエスト・エンド・ガール

namesake.texto: West End Girls (Pet Shop Boys song)[a]

Appearance: West End Girl has a humanoid head and wears a round, dome-shaped cap. It has mechanical segmented eyes, a wide nose, and thick lips. Three small circular piercings or rivet-like nodes are aligned diagonally across its cheek, along with one below its mouth. The Stand's body is long and liquid-like, segmented with vertical lines. Multiple small human-like hands cover its body. It can disperse itself into nearby matter and manifest these hands with long forearms that sprout from the surface it inhabits.
Color Schemes
Abilities: West End Girl is a Long-Range Stand with a maximum range of about 25 meters.
Attacking Through Gaps

West End Girl inhabits and traverses through gaps, no matter how narrow. These spaces act as access points for the Stand to extend its many hands to attack, restrain, or move objects. For example, it has manifested from the seams of suitcases, the edges of stairs, and even the space between an ID card and a person's body. By operating only from crevices, West End Girl stays hidden while tracking targets, ambushing them at the right time. The many small, human-like hands have considerable strength, and can clutch, twist, and apply crushing force. When it enters the gap between two objects, it is estimated to exert a force of one ton or more, allowing it to crush anything caught in the gap.

West End Girl first materializes from several suitcases surrounding Jodio Joestar on Hacca Howler's megayacht, grabbing him by the ankle and twisting it to immobilize him. The Stand then attempts to crush his leg and torso with overwhelming pressure by emerging from every suitcase around him. When it appears from the gaps between Jodio, Dragona, and Charming Man's ID cards, West End Girl is able to sever Charming Man's thumb and forces Jodio and Dragona's IDs into Charming Man's back.
Since the Stand can only attack from gaps, it is defenseless when traveling on regular surfaces.

stands.resumo: Point Blank Seal (至近距離札(ポイント・ブランク・シール), Pointo Buranku Shīru) is the Stand of Mundra featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

ja_kanji.texto: 至近距離札(ポイント・ブランク・シール)

namesake.texto: Point Blank (Bruce Springsteen song) | Shīru (シール) ("Seal", Japanese for sticker)

type.texto: Artificial Non-Humanoid | Psychological Assault | Reconnaissance | Multi-Unit

Appearance: Point Blank Seal takes the form of stickers attached to the soles of its victims' shoes, their clothing, or their bare skin. The sticker resembles an escutcheon, although it is also inconsistently depicted as a rectangle. It has a wedge-shaped top, a French-style base, and a tressure containing a repeating rectangular pattern. A bend within the tressure consists of either four narrow ribands or a single large bend with smaller bends on either side.

At the top of the escutcheon just within the tressure is the English text "KalaKaua AVe.". At the base points are a pair of inescutcheons each inscribed with a Japanese kanji; the dexter base point has 封 (Fū) and the sinister has 印 (In), which individually or together as 封印 (Fūin) literally translate as "seal".

At the fess point is a skull turned slightly toward one side. Beneath each of its hollow eye sockets are two dark markings. The marking on the outer edge is an oblong shape, while the inner marking is a crescent with the concave portion facing a single hollow cavity where the face's nose would be. Its mouth is slightly open with all of its teeth visible and a small rivet-like protrusion near one corner. A pair of hands clutch the head with the fingers slightly splayed. The hands end in a hollow socket where the head's ears would be. Additionally, the fingers have small rectangular markings or protrusions on the backs of each of the proximal and intermediate phalanges. On either side of the crown of the skull are four fingertip-like protrusions pointed upwards that are not aligned with the fingers on the hands clutching the head.

The spirits of the dead appear as the undead forms of deceased individuals, retaining the appearance they had in life. They may also display the injuries present at the time of their death. They are only visible to people currently marked with the Stand's stickers.
Personality: The spirits of the dead speak in a sneering and theatrical manner, using what they find in their targets' hearts to provoke and psychologically torment them. They mock the victims' guilt, sexuality, insecurities, and past trauma, and openly take pleasure in their distress.

The extent of Mundra's control over the spirits is unclear. At times, the voice speaking through the stickers appears to be Mundra's own, as it refers to "my 'Point Blank Seal.'" Other times, the spirits speak as a group distinct from him, declaring "We're the stickers of evil spirits!", The spirit of the deceased boy addresses Jodio as "big brother" (お兄ちゃん, Onīchan), as a child would an older boy. Mundra himself mentions hearing the spirits of the dead, which convinced him to kill a woman for her wealth.
Abilities: Point Blank Seal manifests as multiple physical stickers that mark its targets. Its user initially attaches a sticker to a target directly, after which the ability spreads like an infection to anyone who steps in a victim's blood. When Team Jodio steps in Max's blood, stickers appear on the soles of their shoes. The stickers can also appear directly on bare skin, as two are attached to the palms of Alison Alohaoe.

Mundra describes the stickers as the "boundary line between this world and the next." While a person remains marked, Point Blank Seal can monitor them and expose them to the spirits of the dead, exploiting the spirits' desire to drag the living along with them to the afterlife.
Spirits of the Dead

The spirits look inside the hearts of marked targets, uncovering their deepest thoughts, memories, and emotions. They whisper to their targets, using what they discover to expose their personal secrets and psychologically destabilize them. Among other subjects, they mock Jodio's antisocial personality disorder, childhood bedwetting, and enjoyment of setting a school bus on fire; Dragona's abusive former relationship; and Paco's family history.

The spirits attempt to provoke their targets into turning around and looking at them. Initially, their insults are made to sound as though they are coming from the person whom the victim turned away from, but as the verbal assault continues, the spirit behind them reveals itself as a deceased person. The spirits that appear tend to be recent deaths, such as Max, who taunts Usagi, or some of Point Blank Seal's civilian victims at the Honolulu Zoo's alligator enclosure, who taunt Paco, Dragona, and Jodio, but older deaths can also appear, as Alison is taunted by her deceased husband. The spirits are only visible to the current target of the Stand's effects, and cannot be perceived by other Stand users. As a result, Usagi suspects that he is under the spell of an evil spirit. While Jodio dismisses this, Paco insists that they are being attacked by the dead. Once a target looks back, the spirits can physically attack them. They can pierce or cut their bodies and can also manipulate them into performing dangerous actions, such as entering an animal enclosure.
Self-Preservation

If a marked target attempts to remove a sticker from themselves or another person, Point Blank Seal initiates a counterattack to prevent them from succeeding. It can interfere with the target's perception or use of another Stand. When Dragona orders Smooth Operators to slide a sticker off their shoe, the Stand instead severs the wires surrounding the Honolulu Zoo's elephant enclosure.

Removing an affected piece of clothing does not work because the sticker transfers to the next layer beneath it, including the target's bare skin. Dragona concludes that removing the sticker personally would require sliding away the affected flesh as well.

A sticker can be removed by someone or something that is not currently affected by Point Blank Seal. Jodio initially plans to use the zoo's lions and several lithium-ion batteries created by THE MATTEKUDASAI to remove one, but the attempt fails. Usagi later allows a lion to bite off his left foot, separating him from the sticker. Once he is no longer marked, he can safely peel the stickers from Alison and Paco.

Detached stickers can be physically attacked. Damage inflicted upon them is transferred to Mundra, allowing Team Jodio to hear his cries of pain nearby. Paco attacks the removed stickers with The Hustle, while Jodio strikes his own sticker with November Rain. The accumulated damage causes the remaining stickers to loosen and peel away from their targets.

stands.resumo: This currently unnamed Stand is featured in the ninth part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, The JOJOLands.

Appearance: The Stand initially appears as two long, glowing rods. The rods can bend independently before joining together to form the outline of a simplified humanoid figure. Its body consists of a circular head, an angular torso, and two long legs, with no visible face, arms, or internal features.

During its attacks, numerous small, round protrusions can appear along portions of the Stand's outline. After killing Mundra, its humanoid form separates back into two straight rods, which ascend into the sky. The Stand can also move in its separated rod form, following Team Jodio across the roof of their vehicle before breaking through it and reforming inside.
Abilities: The exact nature, maximum range, and activation conditions of the Stand's ability are currently unknown. It is a long-distance Stand capable of pursuing and attacking targets while its user remains absent from the surrounding area. However, its ability to locate targets depends on an external surveillance system rather than its own independent detection capabilities.
Surveillance-Based Pursuit

The Stand is capable of pursuing specific targets over long distances, including through buildings and underwater. Its appearances coincide with electronic devices located near its targets, which are associated with an external surveillance system controlled by the user.

When it attacks Mundra, he is wearing an electronic ankle monitor. It later follows Team Jodio to a concealed van inside an underground parking garage and attacks their smartphones, despite them being switched off, because the group attempted to avoid electronic surveillance. After the group escapes Honolulu aboard a private submersible, a dolphin equipped with a waterproof electronic device swims near the vessel shortly before the Stand locates and attacks the vessel underwater.

During the attack on the submersible, the military's surveillance operation successfully locates the vessel using a drone launched from a naval ship. Jodio Joestar deduces that the Stand's user is monitoring their position remotely through the surveillance system, rather than the Stand independently detecting their whereabouts. He subsequently uses a speargun created by THE MATTEKUDASAI to destroy the surveillance device attached to the dolphin outside the vessel. Once the device is destroyed, the Stand loses sight of the group and withdraws, although not before launching another attack against the submersible.
Physical Attacks

The Stand's rods possess enough force to pierce through solid structures. They break through the roof of the concealed van while pursuing Team Jodio and later penetrate the hull of their submersible from underwater.

The rods can bend and combine their ends into a circular shape. The Stand can also produce numerous small protrusions along its rods, which it can shoot out as projectiles. Against Mundra, these protrusions appear along one side of its humanoid outline after one of its legs touches his leg. Numerous small holes suddenly pierce the corresponding half of Mundra's body before he is torn apart.

During the attack on the submersible, the protrusions fire multiple projectiles throughout the cabin. After losing track of Team Jodio, the Stand unleashes another barrage of projectiles that puncture the vessel's hull in numerous places, allowing seawater to flood inside.
Paco Laburantes is able to physically grab and strike the rods using The Hustle, demonstrating that the Stand itself can be directly interacted with and bent by an external force.
